4.1.3 Feature Engineering (26 Numeric Features) 
A total of 26 numeric features were engineered from the raw text and metadata to 
capture various dimensions of review behaviour. These features were designed to 
support both anomaly detection in Phase 2 and general pattern analysis. The features 
fall into the following categories: 
Text length features: word_count, char_len, and avg_word_len are used to capture 
the substance and complexity of each review. Punctuation and symbol features: exclamation_count, question_count, caps_ratio, 
and punctuation_ratio are used to understand the writing style patterns that may 
indicate spam or manipulation. Behavioural features: emoji_count, has_url, and repeated_char_flag are used to 
detect informal or promotional content. User-level features: is_anonymous_user and reviews_by_userName can be used to 
identify reviewer profiles and prolific posting behaviour. Lexical features: unique_word_ratio and stopword_ratio assess vocabulary diversity 
and content substance.

7 
Rating-derived features: score_extremity is used to measure the distance from the 
neutral rating (3 stars). Duplicate detection: is_duplicate_text and dup_text_weight flag copy-paste reviews 
with length-weighted scoring. Figure 3: 4.3 Correlation heatmap of engineered features 
4.1.4 Key Findings & Visualisations 
The exploratory analysis provided several important insights. The word count 
distribution revealed that most reviews are quite short, with a median of 27 words.

10 
4.1.5 Output Datasets 
Two output datasets were produced. The file reviews_clean_all.csv, which has 82,069 
rows and 32 features, contains all reviews with processed features. This file went to 
Phase 2 for fake review detection. The file reviews_clean_full.csv leaves out neutral 
(3-star) reviews and includes binary sentiment labels. This serves as another option 
for direct sentiment analysis.

4.3.1 Data Preparation & TF-IDF Vectorisation 
Three labels were defined as Negative (1-2 stars), Positive (4-5 stars) and Neutral as 
(3-star) which was excluded resulting in 72,485 samples (45,379 Negative; 27,106 
Positive). 57,988 training and 14,497 test samples were produced by a stratified 80/20 
split. Using TF -IDF (max_features=10,000, ngram_range= (1,2)) was used to 
vectorize the text which enables the model to capture key phrases like “not good” and 
“very bad”.

results.question: What contamination parameter was chosen for the Isolation Forest model, and how many anomalies did it identify?

contexts:

fewer splits, resulting in shorter mean path lengths and lower anomaly scores. The 
algorithm was selected due to three main advantages: it is tree -based and scale -
invariant, eliminating the need for feature normalization; it has O(n log n) processing 
complexity and completed training within seconds on 82,069 reviews; and it provides 
interpretable anomaly scores and feature significance rankings. The model was 
configured with n_estimators=200, increased from the default of 100 to increase 
stability, contamination=0.10, and random_state=42. Twenty-one numeric features

4.2.3 Isolation Forest — Anomaly Detection 
Isolation Forest (Liu, Ting, and Zhou, 2008) was selected as the unsupervised 
anomaly detection algorithm. This method functions by randomly selecting a feature 
and a split value to recursively partition the data.

31 
This contamination level was selected after testing different thresholds (5%, 10%, and

In parallel, a rule -based detection system was implemented to capture explicit 
suspicious patterns. These rules flagged behaviours such as extremely short reviews 
with extreme ratings, excessive capitalisation, repetitive text, unusual punctuation, 
emoji o veruse, and inconsistencies between rating and sentiment.

This approach reduced false positives and ensured that only consistently 
suspicious patterns were highlighted. Figure 39: Anomaly Detection Output - Ensemble voting results for suspicious review detection 
Several visualisations were used to support interpretation: 
Correlation heatmap showing moderate agreement between rule -based and model -
based detection methods. Anomaly score distribution demonstrating that flagged reviews generally had lower 
anomaly scores. PCA visualisation reducing feature space to two dimensions and showing partial 
separation between normal and suspicious reviews. Feature importance identifying key contributing variables such as behavioural 
irregularities and exaggerated writing patterns. These outputs provided both quantitative and visual evidence of suspicious review 
behaviour. This also shows that  linguistic and behavioural patterns affect more than 
randomness. 7.3.2 Evaluation: 
The anomaly detection results demonstrate that suspicious review patterns can be 
identified using a combination of behavioural and linguistic features. The Isolation 
Forest model successfully captured unusual review patterns, while the rule -based 
system highlighted explicit suspicious behaviours. However, each method alone had 
its own limitations. The Isolation Forest flagged a relatively large proportion of reviews, 
while the rule-based approach risked over-detection due to simple heuristics.

4.3.2 Model Training (Logistic Regression & Naive Bayes) 
Two classifiers were trained and evaluated: 
Logistic Regression: L2-regularised with balanced class weights to handle the class 
imbalance between negative and positive reviews. Multinomial Naive Bayes: Configured with Laplace smoothing (alpha=0.1) to handle 
zero-frequency terms in the TF-IDF matrix.

Figure 41: Sentiment Analysis - Output: Binary sentiment distribution after fake removal 
 
Two machine learning models were evaluated: Logistic Regression and Multinomial 
Naive Bayes. Both models used TF -IDF vectorisation with unigrams and bigrams, 
limited to 10,000 features.

4.3.1 Data Preparation & TF-IDF Vectorisation 
Three labels were defined as Negative (1-2 stars), Positive (4-5 stars) and Neutral as 
(3-star) which was excluded resulting in 72,485 samples (45,379 Negative; 27,106 
Positive). 57,988 training and 14,497 test samples were produced by a stratified 80/20 
split. Using TF -IDF (max_features=10,000, ngram_range= (1,2)) was used to 
vectorize the text which enables the model to capture key phrases like “not good” and 
“very bad”.

These outputs confirmed that the model captured meaningful linguistic patterns. 7.4.2 7.4.2 Evaluation: 
The sentiment analysis results indicate that Logistic Regression is the most suitable 
model for this dataset. It consistently outperformed Multinomial Naive Bayes across 
all evaluation metrics. The high ROC, AUC value (0.9678) demonstrates strong 
discrimination between positive and negative classes, indicating that the model is 
effective at capturing sentiment patterns. The use of cross -validation further strengthens the reliability of the results, as it 
confirms that the model’s performance is stable and not dependent on a single data 
split.

1.3 Scope:  
The scope of this project included: 
• Cleaning and preparing an Amazon app review dataset for analysis. • Conducting exploratory data analysis to understand rating patterns, review 
length, duplicate text, user engagement, and review activity over time. • Engineering behavioural and linguistic features such as word count, 
punctuation use, duplicate text weight, rating behaviour, and VADER sentiment 
score. • Applying anomaly detection to identify suspicious review patterns using
